g 4.1 Framework — The trolleys shall have a welded framework of continuous lengths of mild steel tubes as

avoiding rattling of the glass shelves, suitable size rubber studs or buttons shall be employed and the glass 
shelves pressed on them over the supporting frames in case of curved instrument trolley the glass shelves 
I may consist of two equal segments, if so required by the purchaser The upper ends of the upright

the details shall conform to the requirements laid down in 4.1 of IS 4033-1968*.

AMENDMENT NO. 1 MAY 1993 
TO 

IS 5631 : 1970 SPECIFICATION FOR TROLLEY, 
INSTRUMENT, PLAIN AND CURVED 

( Page I, clause 12) — Insert the following at the end of the clause: 

'or stainless steel sheet of minimum thickness 8 mm contorming to IS 5522 : 
1992' 

{Page 1, clauie 3, Fig. 1 and 2): 

a) Substitute dia of the castor wheel '50 or 80'^r '80' 

b) Delete the word 'glass' wherever appears. 

c) Substitute'MS/Al Cap'/or'MS/Al Disc’. 

{Page 1, clause 4.1) — Substitute the following for the existing clause; 

'4.1 Framework — The trolleys shall have a welded framework of continuous 
lengths of mild steel tubes tubes as shown in Fig.l and 2. The upright members 
shall be connected together by other set of tubes as shown in the respective 
figures. These tubes shall be connected to the upnght members in such a way so 
as to form supporting frames for two shelves, made of glass or stainless steel with 
shaped comers. If glass shelves are used, for avoiding rattling, suitable size 
rubber studs or buttons shall be employed and the glass shelves pressed on them 
over the supporting frames. In case of curved instrument trolley the shelves may 
consist of two equal segments. The upper ends of the upnght members shall be 
sealed with mild steel or alumimum caps. Rest of the details shall conform to the 
requirements laid down in 4.1 of IS 4033 : 1968.' 

{Page clause 4.2, line 1) — Substitute '50 or 80'/or '80'. 

{Page I, clause 5) — Delete the word 'glass'. 

{Page 1, clause 6.2.1) — Delete the word 'glass’
